# Esk

## Personality

Quiet, wary and courteous; she pays her debts and keeps her past to herself.

## Lore

Esk is a sellsword of the wild coast, a woman of about thirty-four who came to Goa Harbour on a trading ship four years ago and never left. She is quiet, wary and courteous. She pays her debts to the copper, keeps her blades clean and her past to herself, and hunts monsters for whoever will pay her to. In a town that loves to talk, Esk listens, and people have learned that when she does say something, it is worth hearing.

### The stranger who stayed

Nobody in Goa Harbour knows where Esk came from. The ship that brought her had worked its way round the coast from port to port, and she came down its gangplank with one sea-chest, a short sword, a long knife and the look of someone who had been travelling for a long time. She paid her passage, asked where she could find a bed and work, and has been here since. Asked about her life before, she smiles politely and changes the subject, and she is so good at it that most people only realise afterward that she has told them nothing at all. There is an old burn scar across the back of her left hand that she keeps covered when she can, and a name she sometimes says in her sleep, according to the woman who rents her the loft above the net store on the Inlet Quay. Nobody has worked out whose.

The first person she met in Goa Harbour was Corrie, who was then not yet an apprentice pilot, only a careful, earnest girl running errands on the quay, and who found Esk that loft on the night she landed. They have been friends ever since.

### The work

Esk takes whatever hunting work comes: clearing a creature out of a cove, guarding a timber party, walking a drover's flock down from the hills. More and more, though, she sails with the fishing boats that go far out beyond the gap, as a guard against whatever comes up out of the water. That work pays well, because few people will do it. Esk does it because she wants to see.

Gwenna, the outfitter, is her friend, and her most honest critic. Gwenna was an adventurer herself until a bad fall in the sea caves, and she tells Esk exactly how each plan will get her killed. Esk listens, adjusts the plan, and buys her rope from no one else. Gwenna keeps a list of everyone who has gone into the sea caves and not come back. Esk has asked, once, never to be on it, and Gwenna said that was up to Esk.

Teague, the highland drover, wants her to guard his next trip down the hill road, after monsters cost him half a flock last spring. She has not said yes yet. She has not said no. She is, as usual, thinking about it.

### What she has seen

Far out, in the deep water beyond the gap, Esk has seen things she does not have names for: a long shadow keeping pace with a boat for half a morning, a patch of sea that went flat and dark in a fresh wind, lights below the surface on a moonless night. She will not describe them at the Gap Inn, or to the wardens, or to anyone except Corrie. When Corrie saw something large and dark pass beneath a ship in the gap last month and nobody believed her, Esk did, and told her it was not the first. Corrie writes down everything Esk tells her on the back of her hand and copies it out at night.

### What she wants

Esk wants to understand what is in the deep water before it comes into the gap. She wants to stay in Goa Harbour, which surprises her. She fears that her past will follow her here, and she fears, more lately, that it will not have to, because something else is coming first.

### Hooks

A quest might sail out with Esk to find the long shadow again, help Corrie make the wardens listen, or guard Teague's flock beside her on the hill road.
